q: Which came first on television: 'I Love Lucy' or 'The Brady Bunch'?
fact: Lucy came first, in 1951. The Bradys did not move in until 1969.

q: Which came first: 'The Ed Sullivan Show' or 'Sesame Street'?
fact: Ed Sullivan started in 1948. Big Bird did not turn up until 1969.

q: Which came first: 'The Honeymooners' or 'The Waltons'?
fact: Ralph and Alice had their own show in 1955. The Waltons arrived in 1972.

q: Which came first: 'Howdy Doody' or 'Gilligan's Island'?
fact: Howdy Doody said hello in 1947. The castaways set sail in 1964.

q: Which came first: 'The Tonight Show' or 'Happy Days'?
fact: Steve Allen hosted the very first Tonight Show in 1954. Fonzie came in 1974.

q: Which came first: 'Dragnet' or 'The Mary Tyler Moore Show'?
fact: Dragnet hit television in 1951. Mary tossed her hat in the air in 1970.

q: Which came first: 'Lassie' or 'Little House on the Prairie'?
fact: Lassie started fetching help in 1954, a full twenty years before Little House.

q: Which came first: 'The Lone Ranger' on TV or 'Star Trek'?
fact: The masked man rode onto TV in 1949. The Enterprise launched in 1966.

q: Which came first: 'Captain Kangaroo' or 'The Muppet Show'?
fact: The Captain opened his treasure house in 1955, twenty-one years before Kermit.

q: Which came first: 'Father Knows Best' or 'The Partridge Family'?
fact: Robert Young came to TV in 1954. The Partridges boarded their bus in 1970.

q: Which came first: 'The Twilight Zone' or 'Sanford and Son'?
fact: Rod Serling opened that door in 1959. Fred Sanford opened his junkyard in 1972.

q: Which came first: 'Leave It to Beaver' or 'Three's Company'?
fact: The Beaver showed up in 1957, a good twenty years ahead of Three's Company.

q: Which came first: 'American Bandstand' or 'Soul Train'?
fact: Dick Clark went national in 1957. Soul Train pulled in nationally in 1971.

q: Which came first: 'Bonanza' or 'Good Times'?
fact: The Cartwrights rode in during 1959. Good Times arrived in 1974.

q: Which came first: 'The Andy Griffith Show' or 'The Love Boat'?
fact: Mayberry opened up in 1960. The Love Boat set sail seventeen years later.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Wizard of Oz' or 'The Sound of Music'?
fact: Dorothy skipped down the yellow brick road in 1939, Maria sang in 1965.

q: Which movie came first: 'Gone with the Wind' or 'Mary Poppins'?
fact: Scarlett came first, in 1939. Mary floated down with her umbrella in 1964.

q: Which movie came first: 'Casablanca' or 'West Side Story'?
fact: Bogart and Bergman met in 1942. West Side Story danced in nineteen years later.

q: Which movie came first: 'Snow White' or 'Cinderella'?
fact: Snow White was Disney's first full-length cartoon, in 1937. Cinderella came in 1950.

q: Which movie came first: 'Fantasia' or '101 Dalmatians'?
fact: Fantasia's dancing hippos arrived in 1940, the puppies in 1961.

q: Which movie came first: 'Singin' in the Rain' or 'Grease'?
fact: Gene Kelly splashed through 1952. Grease did not open until 1978.

q: Which came first: 'It's a Wonderful Life' or 'Breakfast at Tiffany's'?
fact: George Bailey got his wings in 1946. Audrey window-shopped in 1961.

q: Which movie came first: 'Pinocchio' or 'Lady and the Tramp'?
fact: Pinocchio wished on a star in 1940. The spaghetti dinner came in 1955.

q: Which came first: 'Miracle on 34th Street' or 'My Fair Lady'?
fact: Kris Kringle charmed the courtroom in 1947. Eliza reached Ascot in 1964.

q: Which movie came first: 'Dumbo' or 'The Jungle Book'?
fact: Dumbo flew in 1941. Baloo sang about the bare necessities in 1967.

q: Which came first: 'Some Like It Hot' or 'Willy Wonka'?
fact: Marilyn's comedy arrived in 1959, a dozen years before the chocolate factory.

q: Which movie came first: 'Bambi' or 'Sleeping Beauty'?
fact: Bambi learned to walk in 1942. Sleeping Beauty woke up in 1959.

q: Which came first: 'Meet Me in St. Louis' or 'Funny Girl'?
fact: Judy Garland sang about that trolley in 1944. Barbra had her turn in 1968.

q: Which came first: Glenn Miller's big band or the Beatles?
fact: Glenn Miller had the whole country dancing in 1939, long before 1964.

q: Which came first: Frank Sinatra's rise to fame or Elvis Presley's first hit?
fact: The bobby-soxers were swooning for Sinatra by 1943. Elvis broke through in 1956.

q: Which came first: 'God Bless America' or 'Jingle Bell Rock'?
fact: Kate Smith sang God Bless America in 1938. Jingle Bell Rock came along in 1957.

q: Which came first: the 45 rpm record or the cassette tape?
fact: Little 45s arrived in 1949. Cassettes did not show up until 1963.

q: Which came first: Elvis Presley's first record or Elton John's first record?
fact: Elvis first recorded in 1954. Elton John's debut came fifteen years later.

q: Which came first: Nat King Cole's 'Mona Lisa' or Elton John's 'Rocket Man'?
fact: Nat King Cole's velvet voice charmed 1950. Rocket Man lifted off in 1972.

q: Which came first: the Grand Ole Opry radio show or the Beatles' first US visit?
fact: The Opry started up in the 1920s, about forty years before Beatlemania.

q: Which came first: 'The Lawrence Welk Show' or 'The Sonny and Cher Comedy Hour'?
fact: Welk's bubbles started floating in 1955. Sonny and Cher came in 1971.

q: Which came first: the diner jukebox or the 8-track tape?
fact: Jukeboxes were glowing in every diner by the 1940s. 8-tracks arrived in 1965.

q: Which came first: the Model T Ford or the Volkswagen Beetle in America?
fact: The Model T rolled out in 1908. The Beetle reached American roads in 1949.

q: Which came first: the hula hoop craze or the Rubik's Cube?
fact: Hula hoops were spinning in 1958. The Rubik's Cube puzzled the world in 1980.

q: Which came first: TV dinners or the countertop microwave oven?
fact: Swanson's TV dinners arrived in the early 1950s. Countertop microwaves came in 1967.

q: Which came first: the Barbie doll or Star Wars toys?
fact: Barbie arrived in 1959, nearly twenty years before the Star Wars figures.

q: Which came first: the drive-in movie theater or McDonald's golden arches?
fact: The first drive-in opened in 1933. The golden arches went up in 1955.

q: Which came first: the pocket transistor radio or the Sony Walkman?
fact: Pocket radios arrived in 1954. The Walkman came a full twenty-five years later.

q: Which came first: the Slinky or the Easy-Bake Oven?
fact: The Slinky walked down its first staircase in 1945, the little oven in 1963.

q: Which came first: Crayola crayons or Play-Doh?
fact: Crayolas showed up in 1903. Play-Doh was not squished into cans until 1956.

q: Which came first: the Kodak Brownie camera or the Polaroid instant camera?
fact: The Brownie made snapshots easy in 1900. Polaroid's instant photos came in 1948.

q: Which came first: Disneyland in California or Walt Disney World in Florida?
fact: Disneyland opened in 1955. Florida's park did not open until 1971.

q: Which came first: the Oreo cookie or the Twinkie?
fact: Oreos were first twisted apart in 1912. Twinkies came along in 1930.

q: Which came first: Shirley Temple's movies or the Beatles' records?
fact: Shirley was tap-dancing across screens in the 1930s, thirty years ahead of the Beatles.

q: Which came first: Charlie Chaplin's silent films or John Wayne's westerns?
fact: Chaplin's little tramp was already famous in the 1910s. Wayne's big year was 1939.

q: Which came first: Judy Garland in 'The Wizard of Oz' or Julie Andrews in 'Mary Poppins'?
fact: Judy sang in 1939. Julie snapped her fingers to tidy the nursery in 1964.

q: Which came first: Lucille Ball's TV show or Carol Burnett's TV show?
fact: Lucy started in 1951. Carol began tugging her ear in 1967.

q: Which came first: Bob Hope's radio show or Johnny Carson hosting 'Tonight'?
fact: Bob Hope was on the radio by 1938. Johnny took over the Tonight Show in 1962.

q: Which came first: Clark Gable in 'Gone with the Wind' or Sean Connery as James Bond?
fact: Gable had his big year in 1939. Connery ordered his first martini in 1962.

q: Which came first: Jack Benny on radio or 'The Dick Van Dyke Show'?
fact: Jack Benny started his radio show in 1932, nearly thirty years before Rob Petrie.

q: True or false: the milkman delivered bottles of milk right to the front door.
fact: He surely did, often before sunrise, and the empties went back out at night.

q: True or false: men first walked on the moon in 1969.
fact: July of 1969, and just about everybody watched it happen on television.

q: True or false: color television came along before black-and-white television.
fact: Black-and-white came first by a long stretch. Color arrived in the 1950s.

q: A jukebox played what: records or radio shows?
fact: A nickel, a push of a button, and the arm swung your record into place.

q: At a drive-in movie, where did you watch from: your car or a folding chair?
fact: Speaker hooked on the window, popcorn on the dash, kids in pajamas in the back.

q: TV dinners came in what: an aluminum tray or a glass bowl?
fact: Turkey in the big compartment, peas and cobbler in the little ones.

q: A party-line telephone was shared with whom: your neighbors or just your family?
fact: Everyone had their own ring pattern, and everyone listened in now and then.

q: S&H Green Stamps were saved by pasting them into what: books or jars?
fact: Lick, paste, fill the book, then trade it in for a toaster. Pure satisfaction.

q: A transistor radio was famous for being what: pocket-sized or big as a cabinet?
fact: You could carry your music to the beach for the first time. What a marvel.

q: A root beer float is root beer plus what: ice cream or whipped butter?
fact: One scoop of vanilla, and the foam rises right up over the rim.

q: Children's roller skates in the 1950s: clamped onto your shoes or built into boots?
fact: You wore the skate key on a string around your neck so you would not lose it.

q: To change channels on an early TV set, you turned what: a dial or a crank?
fact: It went ka-chunk, ka-chunk, and there were only a handful of channels anyway.

q: Rabbit ears on top of a television were what: an antenna or a decoration?
fact: And a bit of tinfoil on the tips worked wonders on a snowy picture.

q: The Slinky was famous for doing what: walking down stairs or floating?
fact: It was invented by accident when a spring fell off a shelf and kept going.

q: Cracker Jack boxes famously contained what: a small prize or a coupon?
fact: A tiny toy at the bottom of the box has delighted children since 1912.

q: A 45 rpm record held about how much music: one song per side or a whole album?
fact: That is why they were called singles, and why you needed the little plastic insert.

q: At a drive-in restaurant, carhops often served on what: roller skates or bicycles?
fact: Tray hooked right onto your window, and she never spilled a single milkshake.

q: The Sears Christmas catalog had what nickname: the Wish Book or the Toy Times?
fact: Children circled their favorites in pencil and left it open on the coffee table.

q: The colorful Sunday newspaper section was called what: the funnies or the classifieds?
fact: Spread out on the living room floor, read comic by comic. A Sunday tradition.

q: Burma-Shave rhymes were read where: along the highway or in magazines?
fact: Little red signs spaced out along the road, one line at a time, then the punchline.

q: A sock hop was a dance held where: in the school gym or at the library?
fact: Shoes came off to protect the gym floor, which is exactly how it got its name.

q: A poodle skirt was cut how: full and swingy or straight and narrow?
fact: Felt, a big circle cut, and a little appliqued poodle on a rhinestone leash.

q: Tupperware was famously sold where: at home parties or at the county fair?
fact: Coffee, cake, and that satisfying burp of the seal. A whole afternoon's fun.

q: On 'Howdy Doody,' Howdy was what: a puppet or a horse?
fact: A freckled marionette, and the Peanut Gallery cheered him on every single day.

q: 'The Lawrence Welk Show' was famous for what floating on screen: bubbles or feathers?
fact: Wunnerful, wunnerful. The bubble machine was as much a star as the band.

q: On 'Captain Kangaroo,' the gardener friend was Mr. Green Jeans or Mr. Blue Suit?
fact: Hugh Brannum played him for nearly thirty years, always with an animal in tow.

q: On 'I Love Lucy,' Lucy's best friend and neighbor was named what: Ethel or Edith?
fact: Vivian Vance played Ethel Mertz, and those two could get into any kind of trouble.

q: On 'The Honeymooners,' Ralph Kramden drove what for a living: a bus or a taxi?
fact: He drove for the Gotham Bus Company, and Ed Norton worked down in the sewer.

q: On 'The Andy Griffith Show,' the town was called what: Mayberry or Maple Grove?
fact: Mayberry, North Carolina, where the biggest crime was usually Otis letting himself in.

q: Mister Rogers began each show by putting on what: a cardigan sweater or a raincoat?
fact: His mother knitted many of those sweaters herself. One hangs in a museum now.

q: On 'Gilligan's Island,' the boat trip was to last three hours or three weeks?
fact: A three hour tour that somehow stretched out over three whole seasons.

q: On 'Bewitched,' Samantha worked her magic by twitching what: her nose or her ears?
fact: Elizabeth Montgomery actually wiggled her upper lip. The nose just came along for the ride.

q: On 'The Beverly Hillbillies,' the Clampetts moved to Beverly Hills or Palm Springs?
fact: Swimming pools and movie stars, with the cement pond out back.

q: On 'Green Acres,' the couple moved which way: city to farm or farm to city?
fact: Oliver wanted the farm, Lisa wanted Park Avenue, and Arnold the pig watched television.

q: Elvis Presley was known as the King of what: Rock and Roll or Country?
fact: Though he loved gospel music best of all, and recorded plenty of it.

q: Frank Sinatra's nickname was what: Ol' Blue Eyes or Ol' Brown Eyes?
fact: Those famous blue eyes even got their own album title in 1973.

q: Nat King Cole was best known for what: a smooth singing voice or drumming?
fact: He started out as a wonderful jazz pianist, and then everyone heard him sing.

q: Bing Crosby was known as what kind of singer: a crooner or an opera singer?
fact: That warm, easy voice made him the most popular singer in America for years.

q: The Andrews Sisters were what: a singing trio or a comedy duo?
fact: LaVerne, Maxene and Patty, three sisters with the tightest harmony around.

q: Doris Day was best known for what sort of roles: sunny and cheerful or spooky?
fact: She was America's sweetheart, and she loved animals more than the movies.

q: Judy Garland played Dorothy in which film: 'The Wizard of Oz' or 'Cinderella'?
fact: She was just sixteen, and she carried that whole picture on her shoulders.

q: Fred Astaire was famous for what: dancing or boxing?
fact: An early screen test supposedly said he could dance a little. A little indeed.

q: Shirley Temple was famous as what: a child star or a news anchor?
fact: Those fifty-six ringlets were counted and curled fresh for every single picture.

q: Lucille Ball's hair was famously what color: red or jet black?
fact: It was a henna rinse, and the salon kept the exact recipe a secret for years.

q: John Wayne was best known for which kind of movie: westerns or musicals?
fact: The Duke made well over a hundred pictures, and most had a horse in them.

q: Which came first: 'Gunsmoke' or 'Rawhide'?
fact: Marshal Dillon rode out in 1955; the cattle drive of 'Rawhide' began in 1959.

q: Which came first: 'The Munsters' or 'Alfred Hitchcock Presents'?
fact: Hitchcock's droll hello came in 1955, nine years before the Munsters moved in, in 1964.

q: Which came first: 'The Fugitive' or 'Perry Mason'?
fact: Perry Mason took the case in 1957; Dr. Kimble started running in 1963.

q: Which came first: 'What's My Line?' or 'The Price Is Right'?
fact: The blindfolds came out in 1950; the first bids were called in 1956.

q: Which came first: 'The Rockford Files' or 'Hawaii Five-O'?
fact: McGarrett arrived in 1968; Rockford answered his trailer phone starting in 1974.

q: Which came first: 'The Flintstones' or 'Scooby-Doo'?
fact: Bedrock opened in 1960; the Mystery Machine rolled out in 1969.

q: Which came first: 'Kojak' or 'Mission: Impossible'?
fact: The tape self-destructed starting in 1966; Kojak offered his first lollipop in 1973.

q: Which came first: 'Petticoat Junction' or 'Hee Haw'?
fact: The Shady Rest opened in 1963; the cornfield jokes started in 1969.

q: Which came first: 'The Odd Couple' on TV or 'Batman'?
fact: The Batpole slid into 1966; Felix and Oscar shared an apartment starting in 1970.

q: Which came first: 'My Three Sons' or 'Family Affair'?
fact: Steve Douglas raised his boys from 1960; Uncle Bill took in the children in 1966.

q: Which movie came first: 'An American in Paris' or 'Gigi'?
fact: Gene Kelly danced through Paris in 1951; 'Gigi' charmed audiences in 1958.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Searchers' or 'High Noon'?
fact: The clock ticked down in 1952; John Wayne began his long search in 1956.

q: Which movie came first: 'Rear Window' or 'Vertigo'?
fact: Jimmy Stewart watched the courtyard in 1954 and climbed that tower in 1958.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Birds' or 'North by Northwest'?
fact: Cary Grant outran the crop duster in 1959; the gulls gathered in 1963.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Music Man' or 'Hello, Dolly!'?
fact: Professor Hill marched into theaters in 1962; Dolly made her entrance in 1969.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Graduate' or 'To Kill a Mockingbird'?
fact: Atticus Finch reached the screen in 1962; Benjamin Braddock followed in 1967.

q: Which movie came first: 'Doctor Zhivago' or 'Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid'?
fact: That balalaika theme filled theaters in 1965; Butch and Sundance rode in 1969.

q: Which movie came first: 'Harvey' or 'Arsenic and Old Lace'?
fact: Cary Grant met the peculiar aunts in 1944; Jimmy Stewart met his rabbit in 1950.

q: Which movie came first: 'The Maltese Falcon' or 'The Big Sleep'?
fact: Bogart chased the black bird in 1941 and met Bacall's Marlowe case in 1946.

q: Which movie came first: 'Rebel Without a Cause' or 'A Streetcar Named Desire'?
fact: Brando shouted for Stella in 1951; James Dean wore the red jacket in 1955.

q: Which came first: Bing Crosby's 'White Christmas' or Gene Autry's 'Rudolph'?
fact: Bing's record came in 1942; Gene Autry's red-nosed reindeer followed in 1949.

q: Which came first: 'King of the Road' or Patsy Cline's 'Crazy'?
fact: Patsy recorded 'Crazy' in 1961; Roger Miller was king of the road in 1965.

q: Which came first: Ray Charles's 'Georgia on My Mind' or Aretha's 'Respect'?
fact: Ray had Georgia on his mind in 1960; Aretha asked for respect in 1967.

q: Which came first: Johnny Cash's 'Ring of Fire' or 'I Walk the Line'?
fact: He walked the line in 1956, seven years before the ring of fire in 1963.

q: Which came first: the Supremes' 'Where Did Our Love Go' or 'I Want You Back'?
fact: The Supremes hit in 1964; the Jackson brothers arrived in 1969.

q: Which came first: the Ford Mustang or the Ford Thunderbird?
fact: The Thunderbird arrived in 1955; the Mustang galloped in nine years later, in 1964.

q: Which came first: the Diners Club card or BankAmericard?
fact: Diners Club started charging dinners in 1950; BankAmericard came along in 1958.

q: Which came first: Lite-Brite or the Etch A Sketch?
fact: Those two white knobs appeared in 1960; the glowing pegs came in 1967.

q: Which came first: Tang or Cool Whip?
fact: Tang was on grocery shelves in 1957; Cool Whip topped its first pie in 1966.

q: Which Elvis movie came first: 'Blue Hawaii' or 'Love Me Tender'?
fact: His first picture was 'Love Me Tender' in 1956; 'Blue Hawaii' followed in 1961.

q: Which Poitier film came first: 'Lilies of the Field' or 'Guess Who's Coming to Dinner'?
fact: 'Lilies of the Field' came in 1963, four years before the 1967 dinner guest.

q: Which Doris Day movie came first: 'Pillow Talk' or 'Calamity Jane'?
fact: She was Calamity Jane in 1953 and picked up that split-screen phone in 1959.

q: Which came first: 'The Dating Game' or 'The Newlywed Game'?
fact: Chuck Barris matched up daters in 1965 and quizzed newlyweds in 1966.

q: Which came first: 'Laugh-In' or 'The Carol Burnett Show'?
fact: Carol tugged her ear starting in 1967; the Laugh-In joke wall opened in 1968.

q: Which came first: 'The Donna Reed Show' or 'The Dick Van Dyke Show'?
fact: Donna Reed set the table in 1958; Rob Petrie met that ottoman in 1961.

q: Which came first: 'The Rifleman' or 'Have Gun - Will Travel'?
fact: Paladin handed out his card in 1957; Lucas McCain took aim in 1958.

q: Which Audrey Hepburn movie came first: 'Roman Holiday' or 'Sabrina'?
fact: She rode that scooter in 1953 and came home from Paris in 'Sabrina' in 1954.

q: Which movie came first: 'Lawrence of Arabia' or 'Ben-Hur'?
fact: The chariot race thundered in 1959; the desert epic followed in 1962.

q: Which movie came first: 'Cool Hand Luke' or 'True Grit'?
fact: Paul Newman ate those eggs in 1967; John Wayne took the reins in 1969.

q: Which came first: Fats Domino's 'Blueberry Hill' or 'Great Balls of Fire'?
fact: Fats found his thrill in 1956; Jerry Lee Lewis pounded the keys in 1957.

q: Which came first: 'Dark Shadows' or 'The Ghost & Mrs. Muir'?
fact: Collinwood opened its doors in 1966; the seaside cottage series came in 1968.

q: Which came first: 'The Monkees' or 'Get Smart'?
fact: The shoe phone rang in 1965; the Monkees ran onto the screen in 1966.

q: Which came first on TV: 'Ozzie and Harriet' or 'Make Room for Daddy'?
fact: The Nelsons came to television in 1952; Danny Thomas made room in 1953.

q: Which came first: 'Maude' or 'All in the Family'?
fact: Archie settled into his chair in 1971; cousin Maude got her own show in 1972.

q: Which came first: 'The Bob Newhart Show' or 'The Jeffersons'?
fact: Bob started listening to patients in 1972; the Jeffersons moved on up in 1975.

q: Which movie came first: 'Giant' or 'Shane'?
fact: That boy called after Shane in 1953; the Texas ranch of 'Giant' came in 1956.

q: Which movie came first: 'Oklahoma!' or 'The King and I'?
fact: The surrey rolled onto film in 1955; Anna waltzed with the king in 1956.

q: Which Disney movie came first: 'Peter Pan' or 'Alice in Wonderland'?
fact: Alice fell down the rabbit hole in 1951; Peter flew to Never Land in 1953.

q: Which came first: 'The Twist' or 'Louie Louie'?
fact: Chubby Checker got everyone twisting in 1960; the Kingsmen hit in 1963.

q: Which came first: Mr. Potato Head or Silly Putty?
fact: Silly Putty bounced into stores in 1950; Mr. Potato Head arrived in 1952.

q: On 'The Mary Tyler Moore Show,' Mary worked in which city: Minneapolis or Milwaukee?
fact: She tossed her hat in downtown Minneapolis, at the newsroom of WJM-TV.

q: The Munsters lived on which street: Cemetery Lane or Mockingbird Lane?
fact: 1313 Mockingbird Lane was theirs; Cemetery Lane belonged to the Addams family.

q: 'The Waltons' was set on Walton's Mountain in which state: Virginia or Kentucky?
fact: The family said goodnight from the Blue Ridge country of Virginia.

q: On 'The Addams Family,' the bald uncle was named Festus or Fester?
fact: Uncle Fester lit up light bulbs; Festus was the deputy over on 'Gunsmoke.'

q: Elsie the Cow advertised which company: Borden or Carnation?
fact: Elsie, with her daisy necklace, was Borden's smiling face for decades.

q: Mr. Whipple told shoppers not to squeeze which brand: Scott or Charmin?
fact: He begged shoppers to leave the Charmin alone, then gave it a squeeze himself.

q: Charlie the Tuna pitched which brand: StarKist or Chicken of the Sea?
fact: Poor Charlie had good taste, but StarKist wanted tuna that tasted good.

q: The Volkswagen Beetle's engine sat where: under the front hood or in the rear?
fact: The air-cooled engine lived in back, so the front hood held the luggage.

q: Who played Ben Cartwright on 'Bonanza': Lorne Greene or Michael Landon?
fact: Lorne Greene was Pa; Michael Landon was his youngest, Little Joe.

q: Who played the Skipper on 'Gilligan's Island': Jim Backus or Alan Hale Jr.?
fact: Alan Hale Jr. was the Skipper; Jim Backus was millionaire Thurston Howell III.

q: 'Bewitched' aired on which network: ABC or CBS?
fact: Samantha and Darrin were an ABC household for all eight seasons.

q: Who played Gomer Pyle: George Lindsey or Jim Nabors?
fact: Jim Nabors was Gomer; George Lindsey played his cousin Goober Pyle.

q: Madge the manicurist soaked fingertips in which dish soap: Palmolive or Ivory?
fact: Madge let customers discover they were already soaking in Palmolive.

q: Who played Alice on 'The Honeymooners': Joyce Randolph or Audrey Meadows?
fact: Audrey Meadows was Alice; Joyce Randolph played her upstairs pal Trixie.

q: 'I Dream of Jeannie' aired on which network: NBC or ABC?
fact: Jeannie blinked her way through five seasons on NBC.

q: The Impala was made by which carmaker: Ford or Chevrolet?
fact: The Impala was Chevrolet's big, handsome seller from 1958 onward.

q: 'The Sound of Music' was set in which city: Salzburg or Vienna?
fact: The von Trapps lived in Salzburg, with those green Austrian hills all around.

q: Who played the Scarecrow in 'The Wizard of Oz': Bert Lahr or Ray Bolger?
fact: Ray Bolger was the wobbly Scarecrow; Bert Lahr was the Cowardly Lion.

q: Who sang Eliza's songs in the film 'My Fair Lady': Audrey Hepburn or Marni Nixon?
fact: Marni Nixon dubbed the singing, as she often did for Hollywood's leading ladies.

q: Walt Disney's 'Disneyland' show began on which network: ABC or NBC?
fact: It started on ABC in 1954 and moved to NBC in 1961 for color broadcasts.

q: Who played Aunt Bee on 'The Andy Griffith Show': Elinor Donahue or Frances Bavier?
fact: Frances Bavier was Aunt Bee; Elinor Donahue played druggist Ellie Walker.

q: On 'Lassie,' which boy came first: Jeff or Timmy?
fact: Jeff Miller had Lassie from 1954; Timmy came along in 1957 and stayed for years.

q: Who was the voice of Fred Flintstone: Mel Blanc or Alan Reed?
fact: Alan Reed hollered for Wilma; Mel Blanc was the voice of Barney Rubble.

q: 'Hound Dog' was recorded first by Big Mama Thornton or Elvis Presley?
fact: Big Mama Thornton cut it in 1952, four years before Elvis made it his own.

q: 'Twist and Shout' was recorded first by the Beatles or the Isley Brothers?
fact: The Isley Brothers had it in 1962; the Beatles recorded their version in 1963.

q: 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' was a hit first for Gladys Knight or Marvin Gaye?
fact: Gladys Knight and the Pips charted it in 1967; Marvin Gaye's version hit in 1968.

q: 'Rock Around the Clock' took off after which movie: 'Rebel Without a Cause' or 'Blackboard Jungle'?
fact: 'Blackboard Jungle' in 1955 sent Bill Haley's record straight to number one.

q: Josephine the Plumber sold which cleanser: Comet or Ajax?
fact: Jane Withers played Josephine, who always had Comet in her toolbox.

q: 'Ring around the collar' was the worry in ads for which detergent: Tide or Wisk?
fact: Wisk ran that jingle for years, to the dismay of husbands everywhere.

q: Which car had rear-hinged back doors: the Lincoln Continental or Cadillac Eldorado?
fact: The 1961 Continental's back doors opened from the center, a very elegant touch.
